patch.value: Sweep planning: expand a search space into independent child runs

A Sweep carries the search space and the selection rule; its children are ordinary Run items. Independence is the design: two agents can take two arms on two branches and merge, because each arm is its own item and each arm's metrics are history appends. sweep status reports progress and the selection rule's current verdict across arms.

plan expands a declared space into one child Run per arm with the arm's hyperparameters recorded; two arms advanced on two branches merge with no conflict; status reports per-arm progress and never invents a winner the selection rule does not support

value.author: pi-agent
value.text:
Implemented sweep planning and status, to every acceptance criterion.

- plan expands a declared space: `pm rl sweep plan <id> --file --environment --algorithm` takes {search_space, selection_rule}, expands the cartesian product in deterministic sorted-key order, and creates one ordinary child Run per arm with the arm's hyperparameters as its run configuration (verified by reading each child's body and environment edge). The rule is validated BEFORE anything is written (invalid_selection_rule), and every arm id is checked up front so a re-plan refuses (sweep_arm_exists) without leaving a partially expanded sweep.
- Two arms on two branches merge with no conflict: the suite plans a sweep, advances arm 1 on branch agent-a and arm 2 on branch agent-b with a REAL git merge (merge driver installed), and reads both arms' series back through status - the same real-merge proof the run-metric series relies on.
- status never invents a winner: `pm rl sweep status` reports per-arm progress (status, event count, last step, final value of the selection metric) read live from each child's history. A winner is named only when the stored rule supports one (max_final:<metric> / min_final:<metric>) AND at least one arm has measured that metric; ties break deterministically by item order and the tie is stated. A rule of "none" reports "winner: none (the selection rule declares no winner)" even with data present, and an unmeasured metric reports that no verdict exists.

Measured gates this session: npm test 219/219 pass; npm run coverage - 15 source file(s) at 100/100/100 lines/branches/functions, thresholds met; npm run docstring - 15 file(s), 112 declaration(s) documented; typecheck, lint, jscpd duplicates green.

Revert-proof verification: each refusal/guard was temporarily reverted and its pinned test confirmed to FAIL, then restored from git: sweep_arm_exists, invalid_selection_rule (plan-time), the none-rule winner guard (a deliberately reverted status invented a winner and the test caught it), and sweep_unreadable.

patch.value: All acceptance criteria met: plan expands a declared space into one child Run per arm with the arm's hyperparameters recorded (deterministic expansion, pre-write validation); two arms advanced on two real git branches merge with no conflict and status reads both; status reports per-arm progress and never invents a winner the selection rule does not support (none-rule and unmeasured-metric cases state why no verdict exists). Gates: 219/219 tests, coverage 100/100/100 across 15 files, docstring 112 declarations, lint/duplicates/typecheck green. Four refusal paths verified revert-proof.

value.text:
PR 16 round-5 review findings (6 threads), all resolved with revert-verified regression tests:

1. MAJOR — Sweep create outside the arm-cleanup try/catch (index.ts): the final client.create for the Sweep item now sits under the same cleanup contract as the arm-creation loop. If it fails, removePlannedArms rolls back every arm written, so a retry under the same sweep id cannot wedge on the arm pre-check (sweep_arm_exists). Pinned by a late-failing-create test that asserts no arms survive, the sweep id is absent, AND the same sweep id can be re-planned afterwards. Vacuity proof: with the fix reverted, node --test test/sweep.test.ts exits 1 (rl-sweep-late-fail-arm-1 must not survive a failed sweep create).

2. sweep.ts: ArmProgress.final_value is now readonly like every other member of ArmProgress, SweepSpec, and SweepStatusView. buildSweepStatus only reads it.

3. sweep.ts: expandSearchSpace checks the combination cap (products.length * values.length) BEFORE materializing the intermediate product, so a single dimension with a huge candidate array refuses without allocating every combination. Pinned by a new single-oversized-dimension test case.

4. sweep.ts: parseSweepSpec rejects an array arm config explicitly (Array.isArray(config)), since typeof [] === "object" slipped past the old guard. Pinned by a hand-authored Sweep body test case.

5. test/sweep.test.ts: the expandSearchSpace empty-dimension refusal and the parseSelectionRule refusals now assert typed codes via typedUsage() instead of message text, so a code swap no longer matches the old message regex.

6. test/sweep.test.ts: the unreachable create trap and worseCreateCalls counter were removed from failingWorse — removePlannedArms only calls client.delete, so only the delete trap was live.

Gates: npm test 235/235; coverage 100/100/100 across 17 files; docstring 17 files 126 declarations; changelog check green; ./node_modules/.bin/pm health --strict-exit exit 0.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Partial-state wedge from a create outside the rollback region: when a multi-item create sequence (e.g. sweep arm Runs followed by the owning Sweep item) places the final create outside the try/catch that cleans up the earlier creates, a failure on that final create leaves orphaned children with no parent. A retry under the same id then trips the child pre-check (sweep_arm_exists) and refuses — the id is wedged permanently, and the orphans must be deleted by hand. The fix is structural, not behavioural: every create in the sequence must sit under the same cleanup contract, so a failure at any point rolls back everything this invocation wrote. The regression test must assert not only that no children survive, but that the same id CAN be retried afterwards — the retry is what proves the id space is not wedged.
